title: HTMLElement.spellcheck IDL getter: spec disagrees with all engines for ancestor spellcheck=false
body: ### What is the issue with the HTML Standard? The [`spellcheck` IDL getter](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#dom-spellcheck) walks: 1. return `true` if the element's own `spellcheck` content attribute is in the True state, or 2. return `true` if it is in the Default state and the element's [default behavior](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#concept-spellcheck-default) is [true-by-default](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#concept-spellcheck-default-true), or 3. return `true` if it is in the Default state and the default behavior is [inherit-by-default](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#concept-spellcheck-default-inherit) and the parent's IDL `spellcheck` would return `true`. 4. otherwise `false`. For a ` ``` Implementations disagree with the spec and agree with each other: - Gecko ([`nsGenericHTMLElement::Spellcheck`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/dom/html/nsGenericHTMLElement.cpp)): walks ancestors; returns `false` on the first ancestor with `spellcheck="false"`. - WebKit ([`Element::isSpellCheckingEnabled`](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WebCore/dom/Element.cpp), called from `HTMLElement::spellcheck`): same walk, same answer. - Blink: same, via `Element::IsSpellCheckingEnabled`. For the example above all three return `false`. The spec wording has been stable since 2010 (whatwg/html 2953ae89) and no engine has ever matched it on this case, so this looks like a spec bug. Proposal: change the IDL getter definition to match implementations -- an ancestor `spellcheck="false"` makes the getter return `false` regardless of the descendant's default behavior. Filed from Chromium issue [40866451](https://issues.chromium.org/40866451).
